name: Andrej Sládkovič
bio: Andrej Sládkovič (1820–1872), born Andrej Braxatoris in Krupina, was a Slovak Romantic poet of the Štúr generation, the circle that raised the codified Slovak literary language in the 1840s. A Lutheran pastor, he spent most of his later life as a minister in Radvaň near Banská Bystrica.
His love poem Marína (1846), written for his young wife Marína Pietrová, is a cornerstone of Slovak Romanticism, and his epic Detvan (1853) turned the mountain shepherd into a national symbol.
